assessment.nobel_worthiness: Structural empirical methods for demand and competition have fundamentally changed industrial-organization research and practical market analysis.
assessment.attribution: Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes provide the clearest central attribution for the foundational demand-estimation framework.
assessment.maturity: The approach has been extensively developed, applied, and tested across industries over decades.
uncertainties: The broader candidate group reflects important related contributions, making a three-person attribution necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Firm heterogeneity and selection transformed modern trade theory and sharpened the measurement of trade gains.
assessment.attribution: Melitz is the pivotal contributor to the canonical heterogeneous-firm trade framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework is deeply embedded in theoretical and empirical trade research.
uncertainties: The precise scope of joint credit for later extensions and applications remains contestable.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Their political-economy account of trade policy supplied a durable explanation for protection beyond representative-agent efficiency models.
assessment.attribution: Grossman and Helpman are jointly and directly identified with the central theoretical contribution.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped trade and political-economy research for many years.
uncertainties: The empirical portability of stylized lobbying mechanisms varies across institutional settings.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Economic analysis of information technology, networks, and digital-market competition has had enduring intellectual and policy influence.
assessment.attribution: Shapiro, Varian, and Farrell are leading foundational contributors to this body of analysis.
assessment.maturity: The ideas have been tested through successive technological changes and remain central to competition-policy analysis.
uncertainties: The field spans multiple linked contributions and cannot be comprehensively represented by three laureates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative Ricardian models made gains from trade and trade-policy counterfactuals more rigorously measurable.
assessment.attribution: Rodriguez-Clare, Costinot, and Kortum are central to the formulation and extension of this quantitative framework.
assessment.maturity: The framework has generated a substantial empirical literature and is routinely used for policy counterfactuals.
uncertainties: Quantitative conclusions depend on model structure and on the reliability of trade-cost and productivity measurement.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamic-panel GMM methods supplied an exceptionally influential solution to pervasive endogeneity and fixed-effects problems.
assessment.attribution: Arellano and Bond are the direct originators of the canonical estimator.
assessment.maturity: The method is longstanding, widely taught, and supported by a large methodological and applied literature.
uncertainties: Finite-sample weaknesses and instrument proliferation limit reliability when the method is used mechanically.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The systematic measurement of management practices established their importance for productivity and organizational performance.
assessment.attribution: Bloom, Van Reenen, and Sadun are central contributors to the research program linking management to firm outcomes.
assessment.maturity: Repeated surveys, cross-country evidence, and follow-up studies provide substantial accumulated evidence.
uncertainties: Separating causal management effects from correlated firm capabilities and selection remains difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantile regression created a foundational way to study heterogeneous relationships across an outcome distribution.
assessment.attribution: Koenker and Bassett are the primary originators of quantile regression.
assessment.maturity: The method is mature, broadly used, and has generated extensive theory and applications.
uncertainties: Its importance is methodological rather than a single substantive economic discovery.
